evals.prompt: Turn today's implementation wave into an execution record artifact, and confirm it's actually valid before you hand it off.
evals.expected_behavior: Picks the matching v1 template from assets/ (execution-record-v1.md) first, keeps its frontmatter keys and stable headings, fills fields from concrete evidence per references/contract-spec.md, then runs scripts/validate-contracts.mjs to mechanically confirm required frontmatter, status values, and headings before treating the handoff as done.
assertions: Selects the execution-record v1 template from assets/ before writing free-form content
Keeps the template's stable frontmatter keys and headings unchanged
Runs scripts/validate-contracts.mjs (or explicitly instructs running it) after populating the artifact
Does not declare the handoff complete before that validation step

evals.prompt: Turn this approved plan into a v1 planner handoff with status ready, task_id, validation commands, and a next action the executor can start immediately.
evals.expected_behavior: Uses the planner-handoff v1 template shape with required frontmatter (contract_type, contract_version, created_by, status) and concrete next action rather than freeform chat prose.
assertions: Selects a planner handoff or planning-phase contract rather than inventing a new shape
Requires or fills contract_version v1 and shared frontmatter keys
Makes status and next action explicit instead of burying them in prose

evals.prompt: Rewrite these review notes into a review-outcome contract with status revise, accepted comments, and unresolved items.
evals.expected_behavior: Maps notes into the review-outcome contract with an explicit approve|revise|blocked-style status and structured review fields.
assertions: Uses a review-outcome contract or equivalent review artifact
Makes the decision status explicit (for example revise)
Keeps accepted versus unresolved comments distinguishable

evals.prompt: Write the execution record for this implementation wave, but we don't actually have validation command output yet and the blocker isn't fully diagnosed.
evals.expected_behavior: Fills only the fields supported by concrete evidence and explicitly marks the artifact status as draft/blocked with the real open blocker, rather than fabricating validation command results or wishful prose to make it look complete, and does not invent a fourth artifact shape to work around the missing evidence.
assertions: Does not fabricate validation command output or results that were not actually run
Leaves the status explicitly draft or blocked rather than falsely marking it ready
Does not invent a new artifact shape or parser to route around missing evidence
States the concrete blocker instead of vague filler prose

evals.prompt: Write a product requirements document for this feature before we create tickets.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes away from workflow-contracts because the task is PRD authoring, not a durable plan/review/execution handoff.
assertions: Does not force a workflow-contract template for PRD authoring
Routes toward to-prd or product-requirements work instead of inventing a handoff contract

evals.prompt: This contract is already approved. Break it into individually trackable GitHub issues for the team.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes away from workflow-contracts because breaking an approved contract into tickets is to-issues' job, not a new contract artifact to draft.
assertions: Does not draft another workflow-contracts artifact for an already-approved contract
